intro: A population pyramid is a country’s story on its side: the base is this year’s babies, the top is its oldest people. Steer a country through the demographic transition, set its fertility and life expectancy, and watch the pyramid change shape as birth and death rates move.
howItWorks:
The pyramid is computed, not drawn by hand: a population whose women have the total fertility rate you set and whose people survive to each age at the life expectancy you set, settled into its long-run shape. Each bar is the percent of the whole population in that 5-year band (men left, women right; women outlive men at older ages). It is a teaching model fitted to rounded United Nations shares (under 15 and 65 and over) within a few points, not any one country.

Growth rate = (crude birth rate − crude death rate) / 10, as a percent, and the doubling time is 70 divided by it: the same recipes as the course questions (ApEnvCalc). Replacement level is about 2.1 children per woman. Drill numbers are invented for practice and recomputed by a checker on 300 problems per scenario.
